_comment: Curated competitor/partner watchlist for the Competitive & Partner Risk lens. 'role': partner | competitor | both | oem | software. 'threat': High|Medium|Low = current pressure on Printec's channel (INDEPENDENT of size — a tiny local rival can be High on a specific deal). 'tier': global | regional | local-peer = size/reach class. PRINTEC IS ~€15M EBITDA, so 'local-peer' players (a few €m to low tens of €m, footprint-local) ARE real competition — never omit them, especially in POS/acquiring (the most fragmented segment). Cover the WHOLE size range, not just the giants. 'detect' = lowercased name variants matched in signal text. Update 'latest' + 'threat' + 'tier' each week from Agent 6 findings. Do NOT invent; every 'latest' should trace to a vendor finding (find small/private players via tender winners + local-language press).

vendors.name: NCR Atleos
vendors.latest:
The UK CMA (the UK competition regulator) opened a Phase 1 merger review of the Brink's takeover on 26/08/2026. Its legal deadline to decide is 22/10/2026. CEO Tim Oliver now expects the deal to close in early Q1 2027, which is earlier than before.

Because the deal is pending, Atleos held no Q2 earnings call and gave no outlook. A full-text scan of its release found no mention of Europe or EMEA. The only public European figure left is USD 352m EMEA revenue, up 2.9%.

Its ATM-as-a-Service revenue grew 24% to USD 77m. Its count of independently managed ATMs stayed flat at 77,000. This means it is turning bank-owned ATM fleets into service contracts rather than installing more machines.

vendors.name: Brink's
vendors.latest:
Q2 2026 results (5 August) showed group revenue of USD 1,392m, up 7%. ATM managed services and retail cash-as-a-service grew 14% organically. That is the fourteenth quarter in a row of mid-teens growth.

The shift is furthest advanced in Europe. Revenue rose only from USD 358m to USD 377m. Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 59m to USD 71m, and margin from 16.6% to 18.7%. The reason is that Brink's is replacing low-margin cash-in-transit (moving cash by van) with high-margin ATM outsourcing. It disclosed a full ATM outsourcing deal with an unnamed European bank consortium, starting in H2.

The UK CMA opened its Phase 1 review of the NCR Atleos takeover on 26/08/2026, with a decision deadline of 22/10/2026. Completion was brought forward to early Q1 2027.

vendors.name: Mellon Group
vendors.latest:
Audited 2025 group accounts were filed on 07/07/2026. They show revenue of EUR 258.8m (+17%), gross profit of EUR 36.0m and EBITDA of EUR 14.1m (+39%). Net profit was EUR 6.8m (+73%), with 9,606 staff. That is roughly Printec's EBITDA on about ten times the revenue, so Mellon can absorb a thin-margin bid that Printec cannot.

The same filing also records four ownership moves, which matter more than the financial figures. Mellon bought Camelot Sistemi in Croatia outright. It founded wholly owned companies in Ljubljana and Budapest. On 24/06/2026 it completed the buy-out of the remaining 45% of Mellon Cyprus.

Slovenia, Hungary, Croatia and Cyprus should therefore move from safe to contested. There is still no confirmed Romanian ATM win, and its Bulgarian incumbency is unproven.

vendors.name: Euronet
vendors.latest:
As at 31/08/2026, the takeover of CrediaBank's Greek merchant-acquiring business and management of its 141 ATMs had still not closed. It was absent from the Q2 filing, and there has been no relevant filing since 30/07. There is also no notification on the Hellenic Competition Commission register, against a stated Q3 target. That makes 30/09 a hard decision point.

Two earlier readings are corrected. The ATM operating-income squeeze is a non-cash accounting effect of the CoreCard acquisition, and gross margin actually improved to 49.4%. The estate is essentially flat at 57,071 active machines, so growth now comes from acquiring, card issuing and software rather than from taking over bank fleets.

No new European ATM-outsourcing mandate was named on the 30/07 call. Euronet is running a sustained cost-of-ownership campaign for ATM-as-a-Service aimed at bank finance directors, and the third instalment was published 03/08/2026.

vendors.name: Worldline / Cardlink
vendors.latest:
H1 results (30/07/2026): the bank-facing Financial Services division fell 7.1% organically to EUR 363m, with margin down about three points to 18.5%. The CFO put EUR 60m of contract terminations on the full year, half of it already booked by end-June. The CEO said the division will not return to growth before H2 2027.

Two corrections are needed. The disposal programme is finished, and all seven sold businesses sit outside Printec's 17 countries, so the claim that Worldline is leaving the region is wrong. Worldline has also not exited bank digital banking or ATM management.

It is cutting 4-5% of Western European headcount each year to 2030, while positioning itself as digital-euro infrastructure. It was among the 36 PSPs the ECB selected for its pilot on 14/07/2026, taking part through PAYONE in Germany and Austria.

vendors.name: Diebold Nixdorf
vendors.latest:
Q2 filings (29/07/2026): banking net sales fell 6.1% to USD 638.1m, and banking product sales fell 13.0% to USD 236.6m. The filing blames the fall mainly on lower volumes in the Middle East, Africa and Europe. That is the clearest public evidence that its European hardware refresh has softened.

The company is not retreating. It shipped a record number of teller cash recyclers, and its banking backlog is growing. The CEO cited a fleet win of about 1,100 units at a new UK customer, bundled with a long-term service agreement. That is a hardware-plus-service displacement move it will run at NCR-installed banks.

The only named win inside the footprint was a 1,600-unit POS order with a Romanian retailer. With ~USD 60m of buybacks and no acquisitions all year, it will compete on price and service.

vendors.name: Glory
vendors.latest:
Q1 results (07/08/2026): EMEA revenue was JPY 27.3bn, up 27.1%, and for the first time it was more than half of all overseas revenue. Overseas operating profit more than doubled, with margin rising from 5.0% to 8.7%. Management called that step-up structural on 17/08.

The cash-automation arm behind the recycler line Printec resells grew from JPY 10.0bn to JPY 13.3bn. Its kiosk business Acrelec grew about 29%, which makes Glory a self-service kiosk rival in Europe as well as a supplier.

Glory told investors that special demand from the euro banknote redesign is expected from around 2029. The ECB's survey on ten shortlisted designs closes 21/09/2026. As a counterweight, European teller-recycler sales to banks stayed weak, and Glory names no CEE or SEE customer anywhere.

vendors.name: Hyosung
vendors.latest: Hyosung has no direct sales presence in Europe. It is tracked via Mellon, which is its proxy in the footprint. It is the hardware behind Mellon's NBG 700 Series 8 and KAL ATM-outsourcing pitch; note that KAL is now part-owned by Brink's. Mellon Romania has promoted adding Hyosung TNS and KAL to its RO portfolio since 2023, with no named RO bank win yet.

vendors.name: Payten / Asseco SEE
vendors.latest:
H1 management report (31/07/2026): Payment Solutions, the line that overlaps Printec most directly, fell to EUR 102.8m. That is down EUR 5.2m, or 5%, with Q2 down 7%. The ATM line fell EUR 3.4m on lower equipment deliveries in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Montenegro, and Romania was also negative. The terminal line fell EUR 1.9m on lower Slovenian and Croatian deliveries.

This is reshaping rather than collapse. Group operating profit rose 27% in the quarter. The terminal line's operating result improved on growing Serbian recurring revenue. Contracted margin is rising while contracted revenue is flat to down.

This is a company taking fewer, better-priced deals, so it is unlikely to buy a tender cheaply. It bought out minority owners in Bosnia (EUR 8.5m), Slovenia and Serbia. It still has no operating entity in Greece, Cyprus, Austria or Hungary.

vendors.name: Nexi
vendors.latest:
The Central Bank of Kosovo awarded Nexi Payments SpA the TIPS Clone connectivity contract at EUR 685,000. This covers 120 days of delivery plus five years of maintenance, funded by the World Bank. The award was notified on 03/06/2026 and published on 12/08/2026.

Only two bids came in. SWIFT bid 56% lower at EUR 301,138, but was ruled non-responsive because it did not submit the required bidding forms. Nexi therefore won a two-bidder contest by default, at more than twice the rival price.

Nexi is now inside the payments core of a central bank in Printec's footprint, and has a standing relationship with the Kosovar central bank. It also has a path to sell overlay services, which are add-on services built on the payment rail, to every commercial bank in the country. Printec cannot bid for the settlement core, but the bank-side build-out is still open.

vendors.latest:

It holds QTSP (qualified trust service provider) certificates in IT/ES/FR. It also offers automated EUDI Wallet onboarding (PID via OID4VP), ahead of the 24 Dec 2026 wallet deadline.

This strengthens Printec's joint onboarding pitch. The certificates cover IT/ES/FR only, so SEE/CEE localisation may still be needed.

The ownership dispute with JPMorgan has moved past the 'strategic review' stage. The UK case was dropped, and a ~EUR917m claim continues in Greece.

Viva.com is an aggressive, well-funded rival in acquiring and software, and it is now present in two more footprint countries.

vendors.latest:
With Mastercard, PayPoint launched cash withdrawal at its assisted point-of-sale terminals in December 2025. Withdrawals are capped at RON 500 per transaction. This is the cheapest substitute yet for a rural cash machine, and it weakens the business case for dispensing ATMs at Romanian banks. However, a ~35,000-terminal estate is also one of the largest managed-services targets in the country. The right first approach is to treat PayPoint as a customer for telemetry, monitoring and field service, not as a rival.

vendors.name: Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology
vendors.latest:
Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology holds the high-speed central-bank banknote-sorter tier that Printec's product line does not reach. It turned that position into a hard win this cycle.

Banka Slovenije awarded its six-year sorter-maintenance contract to Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH on 21/08/2026. The value is EUR 1,890,000 excl. VAT, on a single bid, and the contract runs to 31/08/2032.

The tender mechanics matter here. An identical first attempt was cancelled on 03/07/2026 after the same sole bidder quoted exactly the same price. The re-tender then accepted it, at +96% on the previous six-year contract of EUR 963,000.

The company is also active at the Croatian, Bulgarian and Ukrainian central banks in banknote authentication and sorting. It is the single source for the Hungarian MNB banknote-processing estate.

vendors.name: Veridos
vendors.latest:
Veridos, the Giesecke+Devrient identity joint venture, won Cyprus' end-to-end electronic travel-document contract at EUR 22,900,450, against a EUR 34,550,000 estimate. It won on lowest price from four tenders, and the award was published on 29/07/2026.

This makes Veridos the incumbent for sovereign credentials, meaning state-issued identity documents, in a footprint market. It is a direct rival wherever national identity issuing touches Printec's digital-onboarding and card-issuing lines.

vendors.name: BOOS S.A.
vendors.latest:
BOOS S.A. is an Athens firm that does bank-branch fit-out, physical security and cash management. It was not on the competitor list at all until this cycle. It won the largest Greek counter-cash-automation contract of the year.

On 19/05/2026 Hellenic Post awarded it a five-year operational lease of 300 banknote counting and quality-sorting machines. The price is EUR 19.25 per machine per month, or EUR 346,500 in total, with an unexercised option for 200 more. It won with Double Power machines rather than Glory, so this was a loss on price and lease model, not a channel change.

BOOS also holds the service contract on Hellenic Post's legacy counting fleet. That affects Printec's cash-automation and field-services lines at the same time. It also gives BOOS a live public-sector reference to bid against Printec at Greek banks.

vendors.name: OpenWay
vendors.latest:
On 23/07/2026 BORICA and its card-platform vendor OpenWay stated on the record that ATM and point-of-sale device management runs on OpenWay's Way4 platform. This is part of Bulgaria's national card infrastructure. That infrastructure processed over 930,000 transactions worth close to EUR 42m in the first 48 hours of euro adoption.

Printec's device-management line is therefore now publicly described as a national utility function in Bulgaria. OpenWay is a structural competitor that was missing from the tracked vendor list entirely.

vendors.name: Datecs Payment Technology
vendors.latest:
On 27/08/2026 the Bulgarian National Bank's Governing Council extended Datecs Payment Technology's payment-institution licence. The licence now also covers cash withdrawal from a payment account, execution of card transactions and credit transfers, and the issuing of payment instruments.

Datecs was already a licensed acquirer with an EU passport and a Bucharest agent. What is genuinely new is the issuing permission and, more importantly, the cash-withdrawal permission. That permission underpins cashback at merchant terminals and independent cash-out deployment.

A Bulgarian terminal maker that owns the device, the acquiring rail and now the cash-out permission can bundle services in a way a terminal reseller cannot match on price.

vendors.name: SelfPay
vendors.latest:
SelfPay, formerly ZebraPay, confirmed in May 2026 that it runs more than 13,000 active self-service payment stations. These are spread across more than 3,000 Romanian localities. It opened 277 new locations in the first half of that month alone. It is heading for roughly 19,000 stations by end-2026, funded by bonds and bank loans. It now also offers local shops an optional card terminal as part of the package.

This cuts into Printec's kiosk and small-merchant terminal opportunity. However, a 13,000-station estate is also one of the largest managed-services targets in Romania.
